findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the S2 acceptance criterion with the HARD STOP: state explicitly that S2 verification runs on a disposable/shadow clone (never on shared origin/tickets) and that 'clean after' means clean on that shadow branch, so the DESIGN+PROOF-only boundary is not violated.
evidence: S2 AC: 'coalescing: reachable commit/tree count reduced; re-signed baseline; enforce_since re-anchored; rebar fsck + replay + verify-authorship clean after'
HARD STOP: 'This slice is DESIGN + PROOF only. No history rewrite / force-push / destructive reclaim executed.'
Risk section hints at reconciliation: 'stage on a shadow branch verified by rebar fsck + full-log replay + verify-authorship'
findings.finding: The S2 acceptance criterion requires measured, verified coalescing output ('reachable commit/tree count reduced; re-signed baseline; enforce_since re-anchored; rebar fsck + replay + verify-authorship clean after'), which reads as executing a history rewrite, but the HARD STOP declares this slice DESIGN + PROOF only with 'No history rewrite / force-push / destructive reclaim executed.' An implementer cannot tell whether to actually run coalescing (on a shadow branch, as the Risk section hints) or produce only a design.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria (S2 line) vs HARD STOP
scenarios: Implementer reads S2 AC and rewrites history on a shadow branch to satisfy 'clean after', then is blocked by the HARD STOP reviewer gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the S2 AC to read: 'coalescing prototyped on a disposable shadow clone (per I9b isolation, never pushed): reachable commit/tree count reduced vs baseline; re-signed baseline; enforce_since re-anchored; rebar fsck + replay + verify-authorship clean on the shadow branch. No origin/tickets rewrite/force-push performed.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the write-fence mechanism and the reconciliation path for events pushed to `tickets` DURING the coalescing→cutover window, so in-window writes (distinct from the accepted >N-day drift loss) are not lost or left un-swappable.
evidence: 'live clones with unpushed writes need a write-fence/maintenance window' — mechanism unspecified
'non-FF force-update of a shared, auto-pushed, high-write-rate branch'
Measured '~14K commits/day' — writes will land during any rewrite window
S2 coalesces to an 'as-of-horizon' baseline; new commits pushed after the baseline is computed but before the ref-swap have no stated reconciliation path
findings.finding: The plan names a required 'write-fence/maintenance window' for live clones with unpushed writes on an auto-pushed, high-write-rate branch, but does not specify the fence mechanism or how writes arriving during the rewrite/cutover are reconciled onto the re-signed baseline (dual-write window / lost writes between coalescing and cutover).
scenarios: A session auto-pushes a new ticket event during the coalescing pass; the force-update swap either clobbers it or the swap is rejected non-FF
Two clones push concurrently during the maintenance window and one loses its write silently
findings.suggested_fix: Add to S2/S3 a defined write-fence (e.g. reject pushes to `tickets` for the window, or compute the baseline against a frozen tip and rebase/replay any post-freeze events onto the new baseline before the swap), and state it as an acceptance criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add (or re-scope) a child owning S2 history coalescing: re-signed baseline checkpoint, enforce_since re-anchor, commit/tree-count reduction, fsck+replay+verify-authorship gate, and the two-clone not-yet-observed-fold test.
evidence: Parent AC: 'S2 coalescing: reachable commit/tree count reduced; re-signed baseline; enforce_since re-anchored; rebar fsck + replay + verify-authorship clean after; two-clone test shows a not-yet-observed fold is NOT reclaimed.'
Roster children: 866f=ADR, e32d='.retired' eligibility (read-only), aff9=stale-clone override, 51a7='removes eligible .retired tombstones + folded companions'.
No child mentions history coalescing to a re-signed baseline checkpoint, enforce_since re-anchoring, or the commit/tree-count reduction the parent calls 'the object-count lever'.
51a7 removes '.retired' blobs, which the parent's Quantified-win section states 'shrinks it by ~0' — it is NOT the S2 commit/tree collapse.
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: Parent acceptance criterion AC3 (S2 coalescing: reachable commit/tree count reduced; re-signed baseline; enforce_since re-anchored; rebar fsck + replay + verify-authorship clean after; two-clone test that a not-yet-observed fold is NOT reclaimed) is not covered by any sibling in the roster.
findings.location: parent AC line 'S2 coalescing…' (no owning child)
scenarios: Epic completion verifier checks S2 done; no child produces a re-signed baseline or enforce_since re-anchor, so AC3 cannot be satisfied.
The '~365-380 MiB' win depends on commit/tree collapse that no child owns.
findings.suggested_fix: Create an S2 child covering commit/tree coalescing to a re-signed baseline (the object-count lever), or explicitly re-scope 51a7 from '.retired'-only to full commit/tree reclamation with the re-sign/enforce_since/two-clone verification.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend e32d eligibility to the broadened commit/tree scope and add the SNAPSHOT-fold (C1) predicate so eligibility matches parent AC2, not just '.retired' reachability+age.
evidence: Parent AC2: 'only SNAPSHOT-folded events whose fold is remote-reachable >= N days are eligible; recent ones excluded; portable'.
Parent S1 mechanism: 'Broadened from .retired-only to commit/tree reclamation (the object-count lever).'

e32d description: 'Compute GC-eligibility for a .retired tombstone: its folding compaction commit has been reachable from the sync remote's tickets ref for >= N days' — reachability+age only, '.retired'-scoped, no explicit SNAPSHOT-fold (C1) predicate.
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: Parent acceptance criterion AC2 (S1 eligibility) is only partially covered: e32d scopes eligibility to '.retired tombstone' reachability+age, but the parent's design broadened S1 to commit/tree reclamation, and AC2 additionally requires the SNAPSHOT-fold condition (C1: 'only SNAPSHOT-folded events … eligible') which e32d does not assert.
scenarios: e32d passes on '.retired' fixtures but the broadened commit/tree eligibility the parent's design requires is never computed; scope-narrowing.
An event reachable >=N days but NOT folded by a committed SNAPSHOT (C1 fails) could be judged eligible because e32d checks only reachability+age.
findings.suggested_fix: Add C1 (fold committed by a SNAPSHOT) to e32d's eligibility predicate and align its scope with the parent's broadened commit/tree reclamation.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-scope the child roster so the commit/tree reclamation lever (S2) is owned, not just '.retired' blob removal which the parent says yields ~0.
evidence: Parent Quantified-win: '.retired files are blobs; the guarded pack is blobless => .retired GC alone shrinks it by ~0. The real lever is collapsing per-event history into SNAPSHOT-anchored checkpoints'.
Parent S1/S2: 'Broadened from .retired-only to commit/tree reclamation (the object-count lever).'
e32d: 'GC-eligibility for a .retired tombstone'; 51a7: 'removes eligible .retired tombstones + folded companions'.
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: Scope-narrowing across children vs parent design: the parent states '.retired GC alone shrinks it by ~0' and broadens S1/S2 to commit/tree reclamation, yet e32d (eligibility) and 51a7 (sweep) implement the '.retired'-only lever the parent explicitly calls insufficient, while no child implements the commit/tree lever.
scenarios: All buildable children target '.retired' removal, which by the parent's own math yields ~0 pack reduction; the effective commit/tree collapse is owned by no child.
findings.suggested_fix: Broaden e32d/51a7 (or add a child) to the commit/tree object-count lever the parent's design mandates.

evidence: 866f description: 'Blocks S1-S3.' and defines 'the horizon config key (default 30d, portable)'.
51a7 deps (from ticket): depends_on e32d, depends_on aff9 — no depends_on 866f.

SCOPE-GAP: backup-ref/rollback/write-fence is out of scope for every child (owned-by-none).
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: Dependency gap: child 51a7 (the destructive sweep) depends only on e32d and aff9, not on the ADR child 866f which 'Blocks S1-S3' and defines the horizon config key both S1 and the sweep consume; and no child owns the parent's backup-ref / shadow-branch / rollback / write-fence machinery that the sweep requires.
scenarios: 51a7 could be scheduled/worked before 866f defines the config key it consumes (ordering/dependency gap).
51a7 executes removal with no backup-ref or shadow-branch rollback child in the roster, so the parent's mandated safety net is unbuilt.
findings.suggested_fix: Wire 51a7.depends_on=866f and create (or scope into 51a7) the backup-ref + shadow-branch + rollback + write-fence deliverables named in the parent Risk/rollback section.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile 51a7 (destructive sweep) with the parent HARD STOP: either move 51a7 out of this design-only slice or gate it behind the escalation/approval the parent mandates.
evidence: Parent HARD STOP: 'This slice is DESIGN + PROOF only. No history rewrite / force-push / destructive reclaim executed. Escalated to the orchestrator for human approval before any destructive action.'
51a7 description: 'The actual sweep that removes eligible .retired tombstones + folded companions'.
container pairing: parent + 51a7-5d9b-95cb-4903/866f-440c-3686-42df/aff9-1252-ad21-4695/e32d-6ea1-029a-435d
findings.finding: Child 51a7 contradicts the parent's HARD STOP: the parent slice is 'DESIGN + PROOF only … No history rewrite / force-push / destructive reclaim executed', yet 51a7 is 'the actual sweep that removes eligible .retired tombstones + folded companions' — a destructive execution child under a design-only parent (conflicting-assumption mode).
scenarios: 51a7 is worked and executes deletion while the parent asserts no destructive reclaim may run without human approval — direct contradiction of the parent's scope gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-parent/defer 51a7 to a post-approval execution slice, or amend the parent HARD STOP to explicitly scope the sweep in with the human-approval gate wired as a precondition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concrete S2 reduction target (e.g. projected reachable object-count / pack-size delta at N=30d) and the concrete W3 budget-bridge value (raise from 100 MiB to X MiB) so both ACs are binary-evaluable.
evidence: 'reachable commit/tree count reduced' — no magnitude/threshold
'confirm the W3 budget bridge value' — value never stated in the plan
Quantified win gives a range: 'Max safe win at N=30d ≈ 365–380 MiB'
findings.finding: The S2 AC 'reachable commit/tree count reduced' states a direction but no measurable threshold, and the Acceptance-criteria health-lane line says 'confirm the W3 budget bridge value' without stating the value or how it is derived. The Why/Quantified-win sections give ranges (365-380 MiB at N=30d) but no concrete target the AC can be evaluated against.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria (S2 line and health-lane note line)
scenarios: Reviewer cannot decide if 'reduced' by 1 object or by the projected ~365 MiB satisfies S2; W3 bridge closes with an unspecified budget number.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'reachable commit/tree count reduced' with 'projected reachable commit/tree count reduced by ≥ <target>, matching the ~365–380 MiB N=30d estimate' and replace 'confirm the W3 budget bridge value' with 'W3 raises verify-identity.yml budget from 100 MiB to <value> MiB'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert on the post-rollback fleet state — define how clones that already force-reset under S3 reconcile after the reclaim ref-swap is reverted (compensating re-fetch/re-reset), not merely that the ref revert completes.
evidence: 'the swap is one revertible ref update' — asserts rollback completes, not the resulting clone state
S3 'stale-clone detection + forced remote-override on reconnect' resets clones to the rewritten baseline
ABSENCE: no assertion on what a clone that already force-reset to the new baseline observes after the remote is reverted to the pre-reclaim SHAs
findings.finding: Rollback is defined as a revertible ref-swap back to the immutable backup ref, but the plan does not assert on the fleet state AFTER a rollback: S3 forces stale clones to reset to the rewritten remote, so a subsequent rollback leaves those clones pointing at objects that no longer match the reverted ref.
scenarios: Reclaim swap lands; a clone reconnects and force-resets to the new baseline per S3; the operator then reverts the swap — the clone now diverges from the reverted remote with no defined reconciliation

a453 AC: '…the growth is reclaimed so the gate is green, with evidence of a passing Verify Authorship Identity run'
Plan AC only asks to 'quantify residual pack size; confirm the W3 budget bridge value + W1/W2 follow-ups filed'
findings.finding: Fitness-for-purpose gap: the named problem (a453) is a GREEN Verify Authorship Identity gate, but the plan concedes its own mechanism cannot reach the 100 MiB budget at a causally-safe horizon, so this slice does not turn the gate green on its own and the acceptance criteria do not make that residual-red / bridge-dependency explicit.
findings.location: Quantified win — insufficient alone; Acceptance criteria (Health-lane note)
scenarios: Reviewers/operators read the AC as 'a453 fixed' when the gate remains red without the W3 raise plus the out-of-scope W1/W2 structural fixes

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the S2 mechanism, name and compare the established history-rewrite prior art (git-filter-repo, BFG, git replace-refs/grafts) and state whether S2 builds on one of them or justify (Rule-of-Three) why a bespoke rewriter is needed.
evidence: Plan S2: 'history coalescing to a re-signed baseline checkpoint = compacted as-of-horizon state + carried authorship_ledger'

Plan lists no tooling; git-scm git-replace docs and andrewlock.net ('Reducing the size of a git repository with git-replace') document squashing/collapsing OLD history behind a graft while preserving recent history verbatim — the same shape as this plan's horizon collapse
git-filter-repo (git-scm) and BFG Repo-Cleaner (rtyley.github.io) are the canonical object-reducing history rewriters
ABSENCE: no Rule-of-Three / anti-repackaging justification for a custom rewriter over these
findings.finding: The S2 rewrite/coalescing mechanism is specified as a bespoke pipeline ('re-signed baseline checkpoint', 'shadow branch', 'immutable backup ref', 'non-FF force-update') without considering or comparing against the established tools that solve this exact problem: git-filter-repo, BFG Repo-Cleaner, and git replace-refs/grafts (the canonical 'collapse old history behind a graft point while preserving recent commits' technique, which maps directly onto the N-day horizon model).
scenarios: Author reimplements graft/replace-based collapse from scratch, missing correctness edge cases the established tools already handle
Reviewers cannot judge whether the bespoke pipeline is warranted vs adopting filter-repo/replace-refs
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art / tooling' note to the Mechanism section: evaluate git replace-refs/grafts (collapse pre-horizon history behind a graft, preserving post-horizon commits verbatim) and git-filter-repo as the rewrite engine, and record the chosen approach with rationale.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground S3 / the force-update step in the established shared-branch rewrite-recovery prior art (fetch + hard-reset-to-remote, push with --force-with-lease) and state whether the swap uses --force-with-lease to guard against concurrent pushes.
evidence: Plan S3: 'stale-clone detection + forced remote-override on reconnect'
Plan Risk: 'non-FF force-update of a shared, auto-pushed, high-write-rate branch'

Retrieved prior art: dev.to 'Rewriting Remote Git History with reset and push --force-with-lease' and SO answers document the standard 'all developers fetch + hard reset to new remote' recovery, and --force-with-lease as the guard against clobbering concurrent pushes
findings.finding: The S3 stale-clone forced-override and the Risk section's force-update restate the documented shared-branch rewrite-recovery workflow (fetch + hard reset to remote, push with --force-with-lease) without citing that prior art or stating whether S3 adopts its safety affordances.
scenarios: The rewrite force-push clobbers an unpushed concurrent write on the high-write-rate branch — the exact failure the Risk section flags — because plain force-update was used instead of --force-with-lease

evidence: Measured '235,482 commits, 408,295 trees' to be reclaimed
S2 AC lists 'reachable commit/tree count reduced; re-signed baseline; enforce_since re-anchored' but no batching/resumability requirement
ABSENCE: no statement that a partially-completed coalescing run is re-runnable without double-applying or leaving the shadow branch inconsistent
findings.finding: The coalescing rewrite operates over a very large history (measured 235,482 commits / 408,295 trees) but the plan specifies no batching/throttling or resumability/idempotency for the rewrite pass, nor what state results if it is interrupted mid-run.
findings.location: Mechanism S2; Acceptance criteria S2 line
scenarios: The offline coalescing job dies partway through 400K trees and must be restarted
A re-run after partial failure double-applies re-signing or produces a divergent baseline
